subject.title: Feature Request: Support YAML as config file format

question: Should OpenClaw add YAML/YML as a supported core config file format, or keep JSON5 `openclaw.json` plus CLI/RPC config mutation as the only core config-file contract?
rationale: Current source and docs still define one JSON5 config contract, while YAML support would add a second parser, filename precedence, persistence, reload, and upgrade surface that repository policy treats as product-sensitive.

options.title: Keep JSON5 canonical
options.body: Reaffirm JSON5 `openclaw.json` and steer scripted edits through `openclaw config` or `config.patch`, closing this only after that maintainer decision is explicit.

options.title: Approve YAML contract
options.body: Require a design and PR that defines `.yaml`/`.yml` precedence, parser semantics, write-back behavior, reload/doctor coverage, docs, and upgrade tests.

recommendation.title: Keep JSON5 canonical
recommendation.body: Reaffirm JSON5 `openclaw.json` and steer scripted edits through `openclaw config` or `config.patch`, closing this only after that maintainer decision is explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent config CLI/docs history makes this the best available owner for deciding whether the documented config contract should expand.
